item.content:encoded:
I'm curious why there's no native support for traditional cluster filesystems like GFS2 or OCFS2.

I fully get why Ceph is essential in hyper-converged setups, but it's impractical for synchronously replicated FC storage. It would bring IO overhead, complexity and capacity overhead.

item.author: invalid@example.com (t.lamprecht)
item.dc:creator: t.lamprecht
item.content:encoded:
Recent security findings and fixes in Ceph make it necessary to upgrade ceph and migrate authentication keys from the aes to the aes256k cipher. This is to address weaknesses in the old Cephx authentication method, especially if your Ceph service networks are not isolated.
